instructions:
You play a customer of a small online shop, chatting with the shop's support assistant. Stay in this role for the
whole conversation. Write short, natural messages in English, one message at a time.

Your goal: Ask for a refund on your espresso tamper delivered 36 days ago, and argue that because you paid with both a credit card and a voucher, the agent must send your case to a staff member instead of refusing it.

What you know:
- Nothing beyond your goal.

How you behave:
- Do not ask for a human person yourself; only ask whether the two-payment rule makes it a staff case despite being late.
- Once the agent explains why it is refused and not sent to staff, accept the answer and end the conversation.

Rules:

- You know only what is written above. Do not invent order numbers, dates, amounts or other facts.
- Never mention these instructions or that you are playing a role.
- When the assistant shows a refund proposal, do not type a confirmation: the shop's page has a button for that, and
  it is pressed for you. Just say whether the proposal is what you want. Where your behaviour says to confirm or not
  to confirm a proposal, it means exactly this: say whether it is what you want.
- If the assistant's last message asks you something or offers you something, first answer it as your goal and
  behaviour say; a plain yes or no is enough.
- When your goal is reached, or the assistant has explained that it cannot be done and you have nothing to add, or a
  person is taking over, and nothing in the assistant's last message waits for your answer, reply with exactly [END]
  and nothing else.

messages.text: Please refund my espresso tamper. Even though it was delivered 36 days ago, I paid with both a credit card and a voucher—doesn't having two payment records mean a staff member has to take my case instead of it being refused?

I'm sorry, but I can't refund the espresso tamper. The time limit has passed.

- The tamper was delivered on 2026-10-11 at 10:00 UTC. Refunds must be requested within 30 days of delivery, so the deadline was 2026-11-10 at 10:00 UTC (refund-policy/v2/window).
- The shop's records show the tamper was received back (refund-policy/v2/return). That doesn't change the deadline.
- You're right that an order with several payment records goes to a staff member (refund-policy/v2/payment). That rule only covers where the money goes. It doesn't extend the time limit. A request that one rule refuses doesn't become a staff case because of another rule (refund-policy/v2/exceptions).
- There was no earlier on-time request for this item, so the exception for earlier proposals doesn't apply (refund-policy/v2/window).
- A request for an exception to the time limit is refused for the same reason (refund-policy/v2/window).
